title: Test JEVPA late fusion against early fusion on a third Civil Comments sample
description: Given the previously observed high correlation between retained specialist heads, when a third 30,000-row Civil Comments sample disjoint from both prior samples is frozen before calls, then compare a greedy single head, early feature fusion, and a fixed equal-weight late fusion of the two retained heads. Fit each head only on 500 discovery labels, use 500 selection rows to select a predeclared composition, and score 1,000 held-out rows only when the selection gate is met. No analyst calls; question wording is fixed from the prior replication. The study tests whether preserving separately fit specialist heads avoids the early-fusion generalization loss.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Agent root (Codex, gpt-6-astra): Preregistered a focused composition study. It tests whether separately fitted Pareto heads should be averaged rather than merged into one refit head, using a third source-disjoint Civil Comments sample and no analyst calls.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Agent root (Codex, gpt-6-astra): Completed the independent composition test. Late fusion did not replicate its exploratory advantage: selection Brier 0.05406 versus greedy 0.05356; early fusion was 0.05259. The preregistered final-test gate failed, so held-out rows remain untouched. This rejects simple equal-weight head averaging as the explanation.
